newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Palestinians set stock exchange framework.
newsitem.headline: Palestinians set stock exchange framework.

text.p: The Palestinian Authority signed an agreement with the Palestine Securities Exchange (PSE) on Thursday, setting the legal framework to operate the first stock market in the West Bank and Gaza.
"We now have the legal status to operate the stock exchange in accordance with its own regulations and rules," said PSE General Manager Safwan Bataina.
The exchange, which has had $2 million invested in its infrastructure, would open "towards the end of the year" but Bataina gave no exact date.

Finance Minister Mohammad Zuhdi al-Nashashibi, at a ceremony attended by Palestinian President Yasser Arafat in Nablus in the West Bank, empowered the PSE to operate the bourse. PSE board chairman Hatem al-Halawani signed on behalf of the Exchange.

"In signing the agreement, we are confident that you have the ability and technical preparedness to administer this exchange," Nashashibi said. He stressed the importance of close monitoring to guarantee the rights of investors.

The PSE said in a statement the agreement empowered it to organise and regulate secondary market trading, supervise the activities of brokerage firms, set eligibility and licensing requirements and impose corporate reporting standards.
It also authorised the PSE to carry out disciplinary actions to preserve the integrity and fairness of the market and to safeguard investors.
The bourse will be run on a centralised order-driven system and has been equipped with modern technology enabling investors to trade and monitor investments from anywhere in the world.
The PSE estimates that up to 65 public shareholding companies with capitalisation of 700 million Jordanian dinars (about $1 billion) will be initially listed on the Exchange.
